create.name: Oren Jay Sofer
create.bio:
Oren Jay Sofer is an American meditation teacher who brings together early Buddhist practice, Nonviolent Communication and an attention to the body. He began practising in the Insight tradition in 1997, learning from teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Godwin Samararatne, Joseph Goldstein and Ajahn Sucitto, and lived for more than two years as a novice in the Thai Forest lineage of Ajahn Chah. He studied comparative religion at Columbia University, qualified as a certified trainer in Nonviolent Communication and as a Somatic Experiencing practitioner, and sits on the Spirit Rock Teachers Council.

His teaching is practical and plain-spoken: steadying attention, growing kindness and equanimity, and learning to speak honestly while listening well. He leads silent retreats at centres such as the Insight Meditation Society, runs an online community, Clear Dharma Sangha, with weekly sittings and talks, and offers self-paced courses including Say What You Mean and Foundations of the Dharma. His books include Say What You Mean, a guide to mindful conversation, and Your Heart Was Made for This, on contemplative practice in hard times, and he co-wrote two handbooks on sharing mindfulness with teenagers. Born in New Jersey, he and his family now make their home around San Francisco Bay.

books.title: Say What You Mean: A Mindful Approach to Nonviolent Communication
books.author: Oren Jay Sofer
books.description: A practical handbook on everyday conversation that pairs mindfulness with Nonviolent Communication. It works through being present in a conversation, finding out what matters to each side, and turning a disagreement into a dialogue, with exercises along the way.

books.title: Teaching Mindfulness to Empower Adolescents
books.author: Oren Jay Sofer
books.description: A guide for adults who share mindfulness with teenagers, written with Matthew Brensilver and JoAnna Hardy. It covers building trust with young people, structuring a class and talking honestly about what matters to them.

books.title: The Mindful Schools Curriculum for Adolescents: Tools for Developing Awareness
books.author: Oren Jay Sofer
books.description: A set of classroom lessons, written with Matthew Brensilver, that adapt mindfulness practice to the needs and interests of teenagers. It is designed as a companion to the teaching handbook above.

courses.title: Clear Dharma Sangha
courses.description: His online meditation community, meeting live on Wednesday afternoons and on the first and third Saturday mornings (Pacific time) for guided sittings and teaching. Members also get session recordings and an audio library; drop-in visits are by donation.
courses.price: $40 USD per month (standard membership; sliding scale)

courses.title: Say What You Mean: Online Training
courses.description: A self-paced online course that goes with his book on mindful communication, open for registration all year. It takes students step by step through listening, speaking clearly and handling difficult conversations.

courses.title: Foundations of the Dharma
courses.description: An eight-session recorded series introducing the Buddhist path, from refuge and right view to intention and mindfulness. Each session has a guided meditation and a talk, and the material can be followed at your own pace.

courses.title: Winter Solstice Retreat
courses.description: A five-day Insight Meditation retreat over the winter solstice in the San Francisco Bay Area, with in-person and online places. Sessions are recorded for registered participants.
courses.price: Sliding scale, plus a donation to the teachers

courses.title: Lovingkindness Retreat at IMS
courses.description: A week-long silent retreat in lovingkindness practice at the Insight Meditation Society in Massachusetts, taught with Yong Oh and Jessica Morey. It can be joined on site or followed online through live broadcasts.

courses.title: Insight Meditation Retreat Online
courses.description: A five-day online retreat in Insight Meditation, with full-time and flexible places and small-group meetings for full-time participants.

free_resources.title: Meditation Resources
free_resources.description: A free collection on his site of articles, talks and guided practices from the Insight tradition, covering common myths about meditation, working with distraction and keeping up a daily practice.
